transcript.text: Good morning everyone. I've called this brief meeting because we have one mobile bariatric lift available for immediate assignment, and both the North and South inpatient units have patients whose transfer plans are being reviewed for use of the lift. Before I can finalize the assignment, hospital policy requires us to hold a brief equipment-readiness check with physical therapy, facilities, nursing education, and infection prevention. I'd like to hear from each of you on your respective areas so we can determine the best course of action.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I'd like to share my physical therapy assessment findings for both patients. The South unit patient failed the sit-to-stand assessment and requires a full-body bariatric lift for every bed-to-chair transfer. The North unit patient can currently complete a two-person stand-pivot transfer with a gait belt. Based on these clinical findings, the South unit patient has the greater need for the bariatric lift.

transcript.text: I need to share an important facilities constraint. The available lift is the Titan-MB model, which has a 48-inch turning radius. This fits South room 412's 50-inch doorway, but North room 318 has only a 36-inch doorway and cannot safely accommodate this lift. Additionally, the charger must be placed in the South 4B equipment alcove. From a facilities standpoint, the lift can only be safely deployed to the South unit.

transcript.text: From a nursing education standpoint, I need to share important staffing information for the South unit. Three South-unit nurses have completed the lift competency validation, and hospital policy requires two validated staff members for every lift transfer. Their available coverage is 07:00-19:00 daily. This means South can support lift transfers during those hours, but we need to confirm that transfer schedules fall within that window.

transcript.text: From an infection prevention standpoint, I need to flag an important requirement. The South unit patient is on contact precautions, which means the lift plan requires a dedicated extra-large sling labeled specifically for South room 412, and a documented disinfecting wipe-down of the lift must be performed after each transfer. We need to confirm that the dedicated sling is available and that staff are briefed on the post-transfer disinfection protocol before the lift is assigned.

commitments.detail: All bariatric lift transfers must be scheduled within the 07:00-19:00 staffing window when two competency-validated nurses are available, per hospital policy.

A dedicated extra-large sling labeled for South room 412 must be confirmed available before the lift is deployed, and a documented disinfecting wipe-down of the lift must be performed after every transfer.
The Titan-MB lift charger is to be installed in the South 4B equipment alcove and confirmed operational before first use.
The North unit patient will continue with two-person stand-pivot transfers using a gait belt, and their transfer plan should be reassessed if clinical status changes.
